correctness.rationale: For M>=5 over C, Casabella–Sammartano prove that the six pairwise-orthogonality quadrics define a prime complete intersection of codimension 6. The Jacobian dependence matrix is a nonzero symmetric hollow 4x4 C with BC=0. Rank B >=3 would force impossible hollow rank-one C; rank B=2 forces rank C=2. Factoring a rank-two symmetric C through a two-dimensional nondegenerate quadratic space yields two disjoint supports, hence either zero column plus dependent triple or two proportional column pairs. Pairwise orthogonality separates the four classes A,T,R,P. Irreducible proper-incidence parameterizations have dimensions 2M-1 respectively (A quadric, T OGr(2,M) of dimension 2M-7 plus six, R isotropic-line dimension M-2 plus two scalars and M-1 orthogonal vector, P perpendicular pair line base 2M-5 plus four scalars). Generic zero/anisotropic/isotropic patterns are mutually distinct; no containment between equal-dimensional families. Independently enumerated every hollow symmetric 4x4 matrix over F3 (729 assignments), finding exactly 116 rank-two cases and zero counterexamples to its bipartite cross-support property. This finite field check corroborates, not proves, the characteristic-zero theorem.
